problem: Operator, 2026-10-26: the spec flow feels weird (propose is only a check, approve jumps into the flow), the page should look and move like the rest of AgentWeave, and it needs better navigation, filtering and ordering (F1044, 'we need to create ordering for the spec'), in the side panel as well, including the navigation used to choose which spec to open. Today the page (hub/ui/src/components/spec/SpecPage.tsx, SpecDocumentPanel.tsx) is a document list, a header with one phase action and a health line, and the document itself as Hub-rendered HTML in a sandboxed frame (SpecFrame), so its requirements and tasks cannot be filtered or ordered by the app; choosing a spec in the panel (SpecIndexTab and the Ctrl/Cmd+K SpecDocumentPicker, both SpecDocumentBrowser) is a search box over a tree with no filters, order, build state or shortcuts; and nothing says what building a document cost or where the time went: the 2026-10-25 post-mortem needed SQL against the operator's database.

requirements.statement: A document's header shows its phase and the actions open to it as buttons: Check while it is being written (never changing its phase), Approve when it is ready, Build or 'Approve and build' once it may be built, with the one the document is waiting for visually primary.
Pressing Check shows what blocks approval and what only warns, beside the parts of the document they concern, without leaving the page or freezing the document.

requirements.rationale: Filtering and ordering inside a document, and showing each requirement's evidence and each task's build state beside it, are not possible in a sandboxed frame of pre-rendered HTML. The operator approved replacing the frame (2026-10-26).
requirements.statement: The document's sections, requirements, acceptance criteria and tasks are rendered by the app from the document's structure, so the page can filter, order, highlight and link them.

The document list can be filtered by kind, phase, text and 'has a build running', ordered by last change, phase, title or roadmap order, and grouped under its roadmap, and the choice persists per project.
Within a document, requirements can be filtered by evidence state and by task, and tasks by status and agent; tasks can be ordered by status or by build order (dependencies).

An outline of the open document jumps to any section, requirement or task; a slice links to its roadmap and to the previous and next slice; back and forward return to the previous position; every position has a link that reopens it.

Each build of the document shows, live: its driver, level and people; tasks by status; wall time split into building, waiting for review, checks and waiting to be handed out; runs; and cost split between building, reviewing and leading.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26, approving the mock: 'don't forget that should be on the side panel as well'.
requirements.statement: The conversation's spec side panel shows the same document, actions, navigation and build progress as the Spec tab, in a layout that fits the panel's width.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'a better navigation of the spec side panel, better filtering and ordering' (approved: 'that's amazing, keep this').
requirements.statement: The side panel switches to any other document from a switcher above its tabs; jumps to any section, and to any requirement or task from a strip that shows each one's state, with previous and next and its position; and filters and orders from one tray whose active choices stay visible as chips that remove themselves one at a time or all at once.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: 'when we open the side panel and open specs we open a navigation to choose the spec to open, I want that improved as well' (approved: 'It works. Perfect'). Attaching stays the composer's control (SpecIndexTab design D9).
requirements.statement: Choosing a spec to open, from the panel's Specs tab, the Ctrl/Cmd+K picker or the panel's switcher, is one picker: a search field from which Enter opens the first match it names; with nothing typed, shortcuts to the conversation's attached document, to documents with a build running (with their progress) and to the last three opened; then every document with the Spec tab's filters, order and roadmap grouping. Opening never attaches a document to the conversation.

The page uses only the app's tokens and primitives, works in dark and light, animates state changes (opening, checking, a build's progress) with the motion tokens, and stops animating under reduced motion.

requirements.rationale: Operator practice since 2026-10-20: mocks are real components, so applying the approved mock is wiring, not redrawing.
requirements.statement: A mock of the Spec tab and the side panel, built from the real components fed recorded fixtures under hub/ui/mock, is approved by the operator before the page is wired to the Hub.

in_scope: The Spec tab's document list, document view and header
The conversation's spec side panel, using the same components in a compact layout, with its own navigation

Check, Approve, Build and 'Approve and build' as the page's actions (behaviour from roadmap slices C and D)
Navigation: an outline of the open document, links between a roadmap and its slices, previous and next slice, back and forward

summary: The Spec tab and the conversation's spec side panel are rebuilt in AgentWeave's current aesthetic, as the rest of the app was: clear buttons for Check, Approve and Build, motion from the app's tokens, navigation within and between documents, filtering and ordering of documents, requirements and tasks, and each build's progress, runs and cost shown live on the document. The mock (task-dadec899cc91, components in hub/ui/src/components/spec/page/) was approved by the operator in the browser on 2026-10-26, side panel included. The same day the panel gained its own navigation (a jump strip and a filter tray with removable chips) and choosing a spec to open became one picker (search that Enter opens from, shortcuts to this conversation's document, builds running and recently opened, then every document filtered and ordered), used by the panel's Specs tab, the Ctrl/Cmd+K picker and the panel's switcher; both were approved too. What remains is wiring it to the Hub as roadmap slices C and D provide the behaviour.
